title: London, the Lake District and Scotland: Edinburgh, Oban, Mull, Iona and the Isle of Skye in 13 Days
meta_title: London and Scotland 13 Days: Lake District, Skye, Iona
meta_description: 13-day UK tour: London, Lake Windermere, Edinburgh, Loch Lomond, Oban with Mull, Iona and Staffa, the Isle of Skye and Loch Ness, by train and small coach.

tagline: From West End nights to the castles and islands of the Highlands

Train, then a guided small-group coach tour in Scotland
Moderate, with two long coach days
intro: A classic first trip to Britain. Three nights in London with a West End show and a dinner cruise on the Thames, two slow days by Lake Windermere, then Edinburgh and a five-day guided tour of the west Highlands and islands: Loch Lomond, Oban, the isles of Mull, Iona and Staffa, Eilean Donan Castle, the Isle of Skye and Loch Ness. Loch Lomond and Eilean Donan will be familiar from Bollywood: both appear in Kuch Kuch Hota Hai. We have updated the original plan for today's London (contactless travel, current shows and cruises) and added realistic train times.

best_time: Late May to early September: the longest days, the warmest weather and every boat running. June and July, as in the original plan, are ideal.
seasons: Long days (sunset after 21:00 in Scotland in June), 15 to 22°C, the most ferries and tours running.

best_pick: Late May to early September; June for the longest days.

faqs.a: This plan uses a guided small-group tour (up to about 16 guests). For a family, we can quote a private driver-guide on the same route.
Yes. Most Highland tours take children from about 5 years old; Staffa is optional for younger children.

faqs.q: Do we need a BritRail pass?
faqs.a: Not for this route. Two advance train tickets cost less than a pass.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in pounds sterling, never in INR. Contactless cards and phones work on every bus, Tube and train ticket barrier. Many places are card-only.

good_to_know.title: Trains and Oyster
good_to_know.text: In London, tap a contactless card or phone at the barriers instead of buying an Oyster card: daily fares are capped automatically. Book long-distance trains in advance for the lowest fares.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and weather
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the three square-pin type G at 230 volts; Indian plugs need an adaptor. Weather changes fast, even in summer: pack a light rain jacket and layers.

good_to_know.title: Tipping
good_to_know.text: Restaurants often add a 12.5% service charge. If not, 10% is normal. Pubs do not expect tips at the bar.

dining_intro: Britain is very easy for vegetarians, and London has some of the best Indian vegetarian food outside India. We send your dietary brief to every hotel in advance.

dining.name: Sagar, Covent Garden
dining.open: Open daily for lunch and dinner
dining.order: Masala dosa, rava dosa, idli sambar and thali. Ask for Jain dishes without onion and garlic.

dining.name: Govinda's, Soho
dining.open: Open Monday to Saturday, lunch and early dinner
dining.order: Daily set thali, sabji and dal. Food is sattvic: no onion or garlic.

dining_avoid: Many British sauces, soups and gravies use meat stock, and cheese can contain animal rennet. Ask for the vegetarian or vegan menu, and say 'no onion, no garlic' for Jain meals.
food_card: We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, ginger, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Please cook it fresh. Thank you.
Jain khana: pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar nahi. Taaza banaiye, please.
